bc_scuitto_bluffs.blurb: Scuitto Bluffs is a small single-pitch crag on the high plateau south-east of Kamloops, up near Scuitto Lake. Fourteen climbs are recorded, mostly trad with a handful of bolted lines and two top-ropes, running from easy fifth-class routes through the middle grades into a few hard 5.12 and 5.13 sport pitches. The climbing is on cracks that come and go and slabby faces, so footwork counts for more than strength. The wall looks south, yet tree cover at the belays and a steady breeze keep it tolerable, and the plateau runs several degrees cooler than town, which makes it a good hot-weather alternative. Expect a long drive in and a modest walk to the base, and little company.

bc_hoods_in_the_woods.blurb: Hoods In The Woods is a roadside sport wall in the Rogues Gallery zone of Cheakamus Canyon, on the highway corridor between Squamish and Whistler. It is the first full-sized cliff you meet there, past two smaller walls, and its short walk from the car plus a deep supply of 5.10 routes make it a busy pick. Thirteen bolted lines are recorded: most sit in the 5.10 range, with a good number of 5.11s and a couple of 5.12s above them. The zone is somewhat inland, so it can be drier than Squamish itself though a touch colder, and neighbouring walls are close together if you want to move around in a day.

bc_the_crest.blurb: The Crest is a bolted cliff in the Chek sector of Cheakamus Canyon, north of Squamish along the Sea to Sky corridor. It holds thirteen sport routes, mostly one pitch of roughly 15 to 40 metres, with a couple of easier 5.8 and 5.9 lines, a solid block of 5.10s and 5.11s, and a few at 5.12. Park at the upper lot and take the short walk up the road, so the approach is only a few minutes. A ledge partway up serves as the start for several routes, reached from the first pitch of a neighbouring line or by traversing in from the left. It suits a mixed group wanting short climbs in the moderate to hard range.

bc_track.blurb: Track is a cluster of boulders at Grohman Narrows, the main bouldering venue near Nelson in the West Kootenay. It sits among the sectors reached by the walk down from the highway pullout, beside the railway line and river. About thirteen problems are recorded, covering nearly the whole range: a couple of easy ones from VB to V1, a middle stretch of V2 to V4, and a heavier cluster of V5 and V6 with a few harder lines up to V9. The area as a whole is known for textured, fine-grained stone, varied features and committing top-outs, and is close enough to town for an after-work session.
